option_checks.evidence: Focus-directed paraxial incidence reflects parallel to the axis, equivalently reversing the parallel-to-focus construction.
Through O is normal incidence and retraces an oblique off-axis line. The proposed axis-parallel result comes from incorrectly replacing O with F.
Equal angles to the pole's principal-axis normal yield symmetry of incident and reflected paths.
The off-axis axis-parallel ray is not along the local normal away from P and reflects toward F, not backward on itself. The distractor mistakes the pole normal for every surface normal.
Focus-directed incidence is not normal incidence through O; it reflects axis-parallel. Confusing focus and curvature center generates the false retrace.
The radius through O is the surface normal. Zero incidence and reflection angles make the ray return in reverse along its own line.
The reflected path starts at P; a path through O would lie on OP. Off-axis pole incidence instead reflects obliquely at equal angle, so equating the reflected path to its normal is false.
Axis-parallel incidence reflects approximately through the concave focus under the explicit paraxial model, with no claim about arbitrary-wide-beam exact focusing.
